title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Join Nurseplus as a Support Worker Make a Difference Every Day

At Nurseplus, every shift you work is an opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of those in need. As a temporary Support Worker, you ll be providing high-quality care across a range of settings, from elderly care to individuals with learning disabilities, mental health challenges, and more complex care needs. You ll become part of a compassionate team where every contribution counts.

Why Choose Nurseplus?
- Flexibility that Works for You: Choose your shifts, whether full-time, part-time, days, nights, or weekends, so you can fit work around your life.
- Weekly Pay & Competitive Rates: Earn between £12.85 and £18.40 per hour paid weekly, depending on shift pattern (higher rates apply for nights, weekends, and bank holidays).
- Workwise App: Take control of your schedule with our Workwise app manage your availability and easily book shifts on your terms.
- Paid Industry-Leading Training: We pay for you to attend our comprehensive, industry-leading training that s in line with the Care Certificate and Core Skills Training Framework, tailored to help you grow your skills, whether you re new to care or have years of experience.
- Ongoing Development Opportunities: From in-house courses to funded qualifications such as NVQ Levels 2 and 3, we support your professional growth at every stage.
- Blue Light Card: Enjoy thousands of discounts on the high street and online with eligibility for a Blue Light Card.

What You ll Be Doing
Your day-to-day responsibilities as a Support Worker may include assisting service users with personal care, safe lifting and moving, administering medication, meal preparation, and providing general companionship. You ll work closely with care plans to ensure individuals maintain independence and dignity, providing the physical and emotional support that they might need to achieve their goals.

What We re Looking For
- You must be over 18 years old and have the right to work in the UK.
- Flexibility in your availability, with the ability to travel to different care settings.
- A good standard of English and the ability to communicate effectively.
- A clear enhanced DBS, which you can apply for upon registration.

If you re passionate about making a positive impact and want to work with a team that truly cares, we d love to hear from you!

About Nurseplus
At Nurseplus, our mission is to make a positive impact and change lives every day. We are passionate about delivering the highest-quality care that truly makes a difference in the lives of those we support. But our commitment doesn t stop there we care just as much for our staff as we do for our clients. By fostering a supportive and inclusive environment, we empower our team to grow, thrive, and make a meaningful contribution to the communities they serve.

title: Care Assistant
company: Hamberley Care Management Limited - Company - Permanent
description:
Be all you can be with Hamberley
At Hamberley, we believe that our residents deserve something 'Extra Special, Every Day' and we're recruiting for a Care Assistant to help us achieve our goals.
At Templeton Place, our Care Assistants are called Homemakers. More than support workers, care assistants or healthcare assistants - they are carers and companions all in one. They have the time to get to know our residents and are trusted to give each person the care they need, in the way they like.
Joining us at Templeton Place, our luxury care home that provides residential, dementia, and nursing care for older people, you'll be part of a team that is genuinely passionate about the health and well-being of our residents.
Working Pattern: 12 hour shifts and working alternate weekends on a rota basis.
We offer our colleagues
- A competitive salary and benefits package
- 28 days holiday inclusive of Bank Holidays
- Quality-linked bonus scheme - A performance bonus tied to our CQC/CI quality rating, rewarding you for helping us deliver outstanding care.
- Workplace pension for your future security
- A true team culture - A collaborative, encouraging working environment where kindness, respect, and professional pride are at the heart of everything we do
- Excellent training and career development opportunities
- Employee Assistance Programme, occupational health and wellbeing support services
- Everyday saving perks - Access to a wide range of retail discounts and savings
- Free on-site parking
- Rewarding connections - Refer a Friend bonus - earn up to £750 per successful referral because great people know great people.

Be different - be a Homemaker
Be at the heart of our award winning homemaker care mode. A Homemaker is a unique caring role for a unique person, where you can care with a difference.
- A varied role where no two days are the same. Homemakers, our name for care assistants, care for individual people in the way a family member might care for someone in their home. We don't do timetabled task-based care - we care for each individual in the way that works best for them. Whether that's administering medication, helping make someone's bed, arranging a family meal with their loved ones or taking them to the beauty salon, you'll always be doing something different. Our Homemakers focus on the tiny details that make our residents unique, and tailor care to each and every individual.
- A chance to make a real difference to our residents' lives. Often healthcare assistants, care assistants and domiciliary care assistants find they don't get to spend enough time with the people they care for to make a real difference. Not at Hamberley. As a Homemaker you have fewer people to care for, but you spend more time with them. It's a more satisfying and fulfilling role that is better for our residents. That's why the model has won awards.
- Excellent opportunities for learning and development. We will support you with all the training you need, including NVQ qualifications and further clinical training if you want to specialise in areas like dementia and nutrition.
- Supportive team environment. Being kind and supportive to each other is key to our ability to show kindness and companionship to our residents. We truly believe this across all parts of our organisation. It's just one of the reasons that, when people join us, they stay with us.

Could you be part of our team?
We provide full training and induction, so we're more interested in you as a person than your specific care experience.
You may have experience as a healthcare assistant, care assistant, carer, home care assistant or domiciliary care assistant and are looking for a different approach, a nicer work environment and a more satisfying role.
If you have no work experience in care but are interested in helping people live happy lives, we'll guide you to a fantastic care assistant career at Hamberley.
What is important is that you have passion, empathy and dedication to help our residents live their lives to the fullest. We will support you with everything else!
If this sounds like you and you're looking for a fulfilling role that makes a genuine impact in the lives of others, this rewarding career is for you.
Due to the high level of interest we anticipate for this role, we may close this advert earlier than the stated closing date to manage applications effectively. If you're interested in joining us at Hamberley, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
About Templeton Place Care Home
Templeton Place is a luxurious care home in Southampton, part of the award-winning Hamberley Care Homes - offering luxury care homes in beautiful locations throughout the UK. Residents live in spacious, stylish ensuite rooms, and enjoy beautifully furnished shared spaces and landscaped gardens. From the deluxe picture house - where we screen classic films - to the on-site luxury spa - offering hairdressing, manicures and relaxing therapies - everything has been designed and finished with the care and attention you would expect from a 5-star hotel.
Hamberley People
We respect and value our residents and each other. At Hamberley Care Homes, we believe in the importance of what we do and why we do it. Creative and empowered, our people see every day as an opportunity for growth and development. We make ideas happen. Together we can achieve anything.
Be part of something special. Be part of Hamberley.

title: Childrens Support Worker
description:
Residential Child Care Worker Just outside of Southampton (Lymington, Verwood or Fordingbridge)

Are you passionate about making a difference in children's lives? We are seeking dedicated Residential Child Care Workers to join a small, therapeutic residential home in Lymington, Hampshire. This role offers a unique opportunity to support children who have experienced trauma, using innovative approaches such as PACE and DDP, within a nurturing and family-like environment.

The Role

As a Residential Child Care Worker in Lymington, Hampshire, you will be a vital part of a close-knit team, providing high-quality, child-centred care. Your work will focus on creating a safe, supportive, and structured environment where children can develop confidence, resilience, and independence. You will build trusting relationships and support children with their emotional, developmental, and practical needs.

Your daily responsibilities include:
- Providing tailored emotional and practical support to meet individual needs
- Acting as a positive role model and fostering trusting relationships
- Supporting children during school runs, activities, and family contact sessions
- Planning and participating in recreational, educational, and social activities
- Assisting children in reaching developmental milestones
- Maintaining household routines, including cooking, cleaning, and ensuring a warm environment
- Completing daily records, reports, and health and safety checks
- Working collaboratively with social workers, educators, and other professionals
- Supporting shift patterns, including sleep-ins, weekends, and bank holidays

Candidate Requirements

We welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds and experience levels, with a strong focus on values and commitment. Essential requirements include:
- Aged 21 or over
- Full, clean UK driving licence (home vehicle provided)
- Compassionate, patient, and resilient with excellent communication skills
- Ability to work flexible shifts, including sleep-ins, weekends, and holidays
- Strong safeguarding commitment and the ability to maintain accurate records
- Right to work in the UK (sponsorship not available)

Candidates holding a Level 3 qualification in Residential Childcare, Health and Social Care, or similar, and those with experience supporting younger children or working in Early Years settings, are encouraged to apply. Experience working with children with complex emotional needs is desirable but not essential.

What We Offer
- Competitive salary up to £35,210 per year, plus sleep-in payments of £55 per night
- Full training, including funded Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare and therapeutic parenting courses
- Support for career progression to Level 4 and Level 5 qualifications
- Health & wellbeing support through an Employee Assistance Programme
- Practical benefits including free meals during shifts, free on-site parking, and discounts via Blue Light Card
- 28 days' annual leave, inclusive of bank holidays
- Casual dress and a family-like home environment
- Referral bonus scheme

Location
Lymington, Hampshire

Apply Today

Please submit your CV, confirming you meet the essential criteria and are prepared to work shift patterns that include sleep-ins, weekends, and bank holidays. We review applications on a rolling basis and aim to respond within five working days.

Vetro Recruitment acts as an employment business when supplying temporary staff and as an employment agency when introducing candidates for permanent employment with a client. Vetro is an equal opportunities employer and decisions are made on merit alone.

title: Female Support Worker
description:
We are looking for a patient, caring, reliable and self-motivated Female Support Worker to join an established and supportive team in Maidstone.

This is a rewarding opportunity to support a young woman with learning disabilities and autism who lives independently in her own apartment within a small, purpose-built setting. She enjoys an active lifestyle, follows a structured daily routine, and values consistency and person-centred support to help her achieve her goals and live life to the fullest.

About the Role

You will provide high-quality, person-centred support in line with an established support plan, helping to promote independence, wellbeing and community participation.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing day-to-day support tailored to individual needs
- Following person-centred support plans and established guidelines
- Assisting with the administration of medication
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date records
- Supporting attendance at a range of social and leisure activities
- Encouraging independence, choice and inclusion
- Communicating effectively with colleagues and professionals as required

Although this is primarily a lone-working role, you will be supported by a knowledgeable and experienced team.

Activities You May Support With

The person you will be supporting enjoys a varied and active lifestyle, including:
- Horse riding
- Going to the gym
- Reflexology appointments
- Shopping trips
- Visiting nightclubs and social venues
- Attending an activity farm for people with learning disabilities

About You

To be successful in this role, you will be:
- Kind, patient and compassionate
- Reliable and motivated
- A confident communicator
- Comfortable working independently
- Committed to delivering person-centred support

Hours:

Full & Part time hours available.

To be discussed at interview

Location:

Sutton Road Area in Maidstone.

Essential Requirements
- Female applicant (Occupational Requirement applies)
- Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle
- Non-smoker and non-vaper
- Full training will be provided, including medication administration and all aspects of supporting the individual's needs.

If you are looking for a meaningful role where you can make a genuine difference while supporting someone to lead an active and fulfilling life, we would love to hear from you.

We may close this post early if we receive sufficient applications before the closing date. If you are interested in applying, we would ask that you do so as early as possible to avoid any disappointment.

title: Support Worker
description:
Job Title: Support Worker

Location: Portsmouth and surrounding areas

About the Opportunity

Due to increasing demand from our clients, we are actively recruiting experienced and compassionate Support Workers to join our growing team, covering a variety of health and social care services across Portsmouth and the surrounding areas.

We have opportunities available within a range of care and support environments, working with individuals who require assistance with their day-to-day lives, including those with learning disabilities, mental health conditions, complex needs, challenging behaviours and other support requirements.

This is an excellent opportunity for dedicated Support Workers who are passionate about providing high-quality care and making a genuine difference to the lives of vulnerable individuals.

We can offer a variety of flexible shift patterns, including day and evening shifts, on either a regular ongoing or ad-hoc basis, depending on client requirements and your personal availability.

Whether you are looking to supplement your existing income, fit work around other commitments or secure regular hours, we aim to provide opportunities that suit your lifestyle.

Key Responsibilities

As a Support Worker, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing high-quality, person-centred care and support to individuals across a variety of health and social care settings.
- Supporting individuals with their daily living activities, promoting independence and encouraging them to develop essential life skills.
- Assisting individuals with learning disabilities, mental health conditions, complex needs and challenging behaviours.
- Building positive and professional relationships with service users while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.
- Supporting individuals to access the community, attend appointments and participate in meaningful activities.
- Encouraging social inclusion, independence, confidence and personal development.
- Responding appropriately to challenging situations, using effective communication and de-escalation techniques where required.
- Following individual care plans, risk assessments and safeguarding procedures.
- Maintaining accurate daily records, incident reports and other relevant documentation.
- Ensuring the safety, dignity and wellbeing of the individuals you support at all times.

You will be supporting individuals with a range of personal circumstances and support needs, so a patient, empathetic, reliable and consistent approach is essential.

Candidate Requirements

We are looking for experienced and motivated Support Workers who are confident working within health and social care environments and have a genuine passion for supporting others.

The ideal candidate must possess:
- Previous experience working as a Support Worker within health and social care settings.
- A valid Enhanced DBS covering both the Child and Adult Workforce. This is an essential requirement for the role.
- Experience supporting individuals with learning disabilities, mental health conditions, complex needs or challenging behaviours.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive relationships.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a wider care and support team.
- High levels of emotional resilience, patience, empathy and understanding.
- The ability to remain calm, professional and proactive when dealing with challenging situations.
- An understanding of safeguarding, duty of care, confidentiality and professional boundaries.
- A flexible, reliable and responsible approach to work.
- A genuine commitment to promoting independence, dignity and person-centred care.

What We Offer

We recognise the importance of our Support Workers and are committed to providing competitive benefits alongside ongoing support and development.
- Competitive hourly rates of pay.
- Weekly pay via BACS.
- Holiday pay accrued separately, on top of your hourly rate.
- Access to mandatory training and recognised certificates to support your continued professional development.
- Optional workplace pension scheme.

You will also benefit from ongoing support from our experienced Health & Social Care Consultants, including:
- Detailed information and briefings about each service before your first shift.
- Additional supervised support and training where required or requested.
- Opportunities for continued professional development and up-skilling.
- A dedicated team of experienced consultants available to assist with shifts and placements.
- 24/7 out-of-hours support, ensuring guidance is available when needed.

Terms and conditions apply.

Kingdom People is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

Right to Work in the UK

Please note that Kingdom People is unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must already have the unrestricted right to work in the UK or hold a valid visa sponsored by another employer that permits them to undertake this work. Evidence of the right to work in the UK will be required.

Whether you re supporting individuals with learning disabilities, complex care needs, mental health conditions, dementia, or assisting elderly clients, you ll be making a meaningful difference with every shift.

Why Join Nurseplus Care at home?
- Continuity of Care: We strive to provide continuity with the same clients and consistent hours each week. Whether you prefer short visits traveling from home to home or longer 12-hour shifts in one location, we have a variety of options to suit your lifestyle.
- Weekly Pay & Competitive Rates: Earn between £14.57 and £21.29 per hour, paid weekly, depending on shift pattern (higher rates apply for nights, weekends, and bank holidays).
- Deliver Compassionate Care: Make a lasting impact by helping clients live independently and with dignity, through companionship, personal care, medication administration, and more, all guided by personalised care plans.
- Tailored Client Matching: We believe in matching you with clients that align with your skills and passions. Whether you're looking to support individuals with mental health needs, learning disabilities, children, or older adults, we work to pair you with the clients you feel most comfortable and confident working with.
- Paid Industry-Leading Training: We pay for you to attend our comprehensive, industry-leading training that s in line with the Care Certificate and Core Skills Training Framework, tailored to help you grow your skills, whether you re new to care or have years of experience.
- Ongoing Development: Benefit from continuous support and development opportunities, including in-house courses and funded qualifications like NVQ Levels 2 and 3.
- Blue Light Card: Enjoy thousands of discounts on the high street and online with eligibility for a Blue Light Card.

What You ll Be Doing

As a Homecare Assistant, your role is vital to improving the quality of life of those you support. You ll provide personal care, assist with nutritional needs, administer medication, and offer companionship ensuring clients feel valued and cared for in their own homes. All care is delivered in accordance with each client's individual care plan, tailored to their needs.

What We re Looking For
- You must be over 18 years old and have the right to work in the UK.
- A full UK driving licence is essential.
- Strong communication skills and a good standard of English are required.
- You ll need an enhanced DBS, which you can apply for upon registration.
- We are looking to cover 14:00 - 22:00 shift

If you're ready to deliver outstanding care in the community and make a real difference, we d love to welcome you to our dedicated Nurseplus Care at home team!

About Nurseplus

At Nurseplus, our mission is to make a positive impact and change lives every day. We are passionate about delivering the highest-quality care that truly makes a difference in the lives of those we support. But our commitment doesn t stop there we care just as much for our staff as we do for our clients. By fostering a supportive and inclusive environment, we empower our team to grow, thrive, and make a meaningful contribution to the communities they serve.

Be different - be a Homemaker
Be at the heart of our award winning homemaker care mode. A Homemaker is a unique caring role for a unique person, where you can care with a difference.
- A varied role where no two days are the same. Homemakers, our name for care assistants, care for individual people in the way a family member might care for someone in their home. We don't do timetabled task-based care - we care for each individual in the way that works best for them. Whether that's administering medication, helping make someone's bed, arranging a family meal with their loved ones or taking them to the beauty salon, you'll always be doing something different. Our Homemakers focus on the tiny details that make our residents unique, and tailor care to each and every individual.
- A chance to make a real difference to our residents' lives. Often healthcare assistants, care assistants and domiciliary care assistants find they don't get to spend enough time with the people they care for to make a real difference. Not at Hamberley. As a Homemaker you have fewer people to care for, but you spend more time with them. It's a more satisfying and fulfilling role that is better for our residents. That's why the model has won awards.
- Excellent opportunities for learning and development. We will support you with all the training you need, including NVQ qualifications and further clinical training if you want to specialise in areas like dementia and nutrition.
- Supportive team environment. Being kind and supportive to each other is key to our ability to show kindness and companionship to our residents. We truly believe this across all parts of our organisation. It's just one of the reasons that, when people join us, they stay with us.
